newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thousands stranded in Singapore by Indian strike.
newsitem.headline: Thousands stranded in Singapore by Indian strike.

text.p: Up to 3,000 passengers were forced to spend the night in Singapore because of a nationwide strike by Indian air traffic controllers, Singapore Airlines (SIA) said on Saturday.

An SIA spokeswoman said the airline suspended 13 flights to 12 destinations in India, the Middle East and Europe on Friday because of the strike. She said the impact would be about the same on Saturday.
SIA said in a statement that disruption to its flights began after it was informed of the situation at 0615 GMT on Friday.
The airline was only able to find accommodation for about 1,000 passengers stranded in Singapore on Friday night.
"Unfortunately we were unable to find accommodation for a further 2,000, some of whom spent the night at (Changi) airport. We provided food and blankets for those passengers," the statement said.
SIA said it was trying to obtain seats for stranded passengers on other airlines and applying for approval to operate over other routings that avoid Indian airspace.

Indian air traffic controllers went on strike to protest against the suspension of a colleague, officials from the Airports Authority of India said. Officials said the employee was punished for a lapse that could have resulted in a mid-air collision.

The world's worst mid-air collision occurred over New Delhi's skies in November between a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter, killing all 349 people on the two planes.
